item.title: The Tape: the week of 16 to 22 November 2026
item.content:encoded:
3 episodes, 51 stories, 100 minutes of listening.

The Ticker

At Wednesday's close, the S&P 500 finished at 7,324, down 0.2 percent. The Nasdaq Composite was up 0.4 percent and the Dow was down 1.1 percent. And in big tech, Amazon had the best day, up 3.8 percent, while Nvidia was at the other end, down 2.9 percent. That's a snapshot, not advice.

First Tick

New AI‑native CRM challenges giants, plus Uber and Zoox hit the streets together

Episode 2 · Tue 17 Nov · 34 min

  • Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM (TechCrunch)
  • Zoox robotaxis are now on the Uber app in Las Vegas (TechCrunch)
  • Senator slams Commerce Secretary for flow of Nvidia AI chips to China (The Verge)
  • Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors (Ars Technica)
  • Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang (TechCrunch)
  • Where was Nvidia’s security team? (TechCrunch)
  • The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it (TechCrunch)
  • Three questions for anyone considering the Nvidia CEO job (MarketWatch)
  • ‘Standing on one leg’: IMF chief warns about global economy as AI circular financing hits $1 trillion (CNBC)
  • Nvidia's Colette Kress confronts key questions in first earnings report since Jensen Huang’s exit (CNBC)
  • Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber (The Verge)
  • Nvidia stock falls nearly 4% as investors price in fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation (CNBC)
  • Vulcan rocket fails, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites (The Verge)
  • The tech world's calls for Jensen Huang to return to Nvidia are growing (CNBC)
  • Delivery drones are coming. For some with PTSD, that's a terrifying prospect. (Ars Technica)
  • Nvidia shares under pressure as calls grow for Huang to be reinstated as CEO (CNBC)

The Takeaway

Maya I think the biggest thread connecting all this chaos is just how quickly things can shift in the AI space—a rocket failure, a CEO stepping down, a trillion dollars circling—it's all moving so fast.

Alex Yeah. It’s a stark reminder that building anything real is hard, regardless of how much hype there is. Makes you wonder what's genuinely solid.

Listen, or read the transcript

First Tick

Nvidia keeps open‑source plans alive, plus Nvidia rejects founder’s return offer

Episode 3 · Wed 18 Nov · 33 min

  • Nvidia says its open-source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit (TechCrunch)
  • Nvidia says it doesn’t plan to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO (TechCrunch)
  • Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO (TechCrunch)
  • Waymo suspends freeway rides nationwide after California DMV order (TechCrunch)
  • Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer (MIT Technology Review)
  • Isomorphic Labs raises $5B as it looks to take drug candidates to clinical trials (TechCrunch)
  • Nvidia’s first big move after Jensen Huang’s exit targets national security (TechCrunch)
  • Widespread outages hit banks, air travel, the NSA and Apple, disrupting seemingly everything (CNBC)
  • Nvidia closes lower ahead of earnings as company reels from Huang resignation (CNBC)
  • Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he’s open to returning in first statement since resignation (CNBC)
  • Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense (Ars Technica)
  • Science Corporation’s brain tech is worth $3.5 billion after new funding (TechCrunch)
  • Analysis: The Fed's chairman sees an AI revolution coming. Now he has to figure out what it means (CNBC)
  • Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors (Ars Technica)
  • Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free (The Verge)
  • Demis Hassabis’ AI company raises $5 billion, months after he left as Google DeepMind CEO (CNBC)
  • Apple services, including iCloud, App Store, Apple Music, and more, hit by outage (TechCrunch)

The Takeaway

Maya The kicker is that Nvidia’s exit and the Anthropic stake shift both point to a market pivot toward AI governance.

Alex If Nvidia’s staying open‑source, they’re betting on community trust, not just chips.

Listen, or read the transcript

First Tick

Elon backs Jensen like a superstar, plus Committee votes despite boycott

Episode 4 · Thu 19 Nov · 33 min

  • Elon Musk says ousting Jensen Huang is like ‘kicking Michael Jordan off your team’ (TechCrunch)
  • Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote (Ars Technica)
  • Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits (Ars Technica)
  • Satya Nadella predicts AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web (TechCrunch)
  • Nvidia isn’t selling any more AI chips to China (The Verge)
  • Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster (TechCrunch)
  • Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt (TechCrunch)
  • Anthropic prices IPO at $83 per share, above expected range, source tells CNBC (CNBC)
  • Retail investor enthusiasm for Anthropic IPO to rival SpaceX debut (CNBC)
  • Palo Alto inks $4.5 billion deal for AI startup Applied Compute, shares pop 7% on earnings (CNBC)
  • Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella remains confident in Nvidia after Huang’s exit (TechCrunch)
  • India’s Humyn Labs raises $47M to feed US robotics companies the data they need (TechCrunch)
  • One of AI's most notorious 'doomers' stands to make billions in Anthropic's IPO (CNBC)
  • Anthropic reportedly prices IPO at $83 a share, above projected range (TechCrunch)
  • Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now (TechCrunch)
  • Nvidia sinks after earnings, dragging down neoclouds CoreWeave, Iren (CNBC)
  • Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick (Ars Technica)
  • The DOJ says it’s investigating Megaspeed (The Verge)

The Takeaway

Maya The real riff here is whether Nvidia’s pull‑back will still make the market lean on AI chips.

Alex Yeah, if they keep walking away from China, the supply chain will bite more than the headline buzz.

item.title: The Tape: the week of 9 to 15 November 2026
item.content:encoded:
2 episodes, 11 stories, 24 minutes of listening.

The Ticker

At Wednesday's close, the S&P 500 finished at 7,619, up 1.3 percent. The Nasdaq Composite was up 1.6 percent and the Dow was up 0.5 percent. And in big tech, Tesla had the best day, up 2.9 percent, while Microsoft was at the other end, down 2.3 percent. That's a snapshot, not advice.

The Brief

Satellites seeing in the dark now apparently, plus Chips meet AI in a surprising deal

Episode 1 · Thu 12 Nov · 8 min

  • Anduril says its first satellite can see adversaries maneuver in orbital night (Ars Technica)
  • Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI (Ars Technica)
  • All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO (TechCrunch)
  • ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’ (The Verge)
  • Meta head of infrastructure will leave and be succeeded by former AWS cloud exec (CNBC)
  • Jim Cramer says investors need to pay attention to CoreWeave. Here's why (CNBC)

The Takeaway

Alex I just think the satellite stuff—seeing maneuvers in orbit—sounds like a massive engineering challenge, even if it’s a demo.

Maya I’m going to be watching how quickly those Business Agents for ChatGPT start impacting actual productivity and, crucially, the bottom line for those businesses.

Listen, or read the transcript

The Breakdown

New VC fund trying to break through, plus AI revenue numbers just went ballistic

Episode 2 · Thu 12 Nov · 16 min

  • Olaf Sakkers is betting he can beat the emerging-manager squeeze (TechCrunch)
  • OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time (TechCrunch)
  • Adobe’s AI experiments let you walk around in photos and interview your characters (The Verge)
  • PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery (TechCrunch)
  • Analysis: Is Nvidia too big to fail? Its AI financing web raises the stakes (CNBC)

The Takeaway

Maya I think the common thread here is just how much money is sloshing around, enabling all this experimentation, right?

Alex I'll be watching to see how quickly those Adobe AI features actually ship – demos are easy.
